name: Reporting File Information (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that receives the full path to an input file from the user, reads that file and reports the number of lines, the longest line, the number of words on each line, and the length of the longest word on each line. Make sure that the program handles each specific exception that could occur. Also, the program must ask the user for a valid file path until the user enters a file path that could be accessed without any exception.
code:
#Step 1: Define the function that gets the valid file path
def get_file():
    valid = False
    while not valid : 
        try:
            file_name = input("Enter the full path of a file: ")
            myfile = open( file_name, "r") 
            myfile.close()
            valid = True
        except FileNotFoundError:
            print("File not found.")
        except IOError:
            print("Problem with the file!")
    return file_name
#Step 2: Define the function that processes the file
def get_stat(file_name):
    #Step 2.1: Assign initial value to variable that we need for reporting the file information
    num_lines = 0
    longest_line = ""
    #Step 2.2: Enclose the code that might throw an exception within the try block
    try :
        #Step 2.2.1: Open the file and process each line in the file
        myfile = open( file_name, "r")
        for line in myfile:
            num_lines += 1
            num_words = len(line.split())
            #Determine if the line is the longest line so far
            if (len(line) > len(longest_line)) :
                longest_line = line
            #Find the length of the longest word in the line
            longest_word = 0
            for w in line.split() :
                if len(w) > longest_word :
                    longest_word = len(w)
            #Print the line information
            print("Line " + str(num_lines) + " has " + str(num_words) + " tokens (longest = " + str(longest_word) + ")")
        print("Longest line:" + longest_line)
        #Step 2.2.2: Close the file
        myfile.close()
    #Step 2.3: Handle all possible exceptions that may be thrown in the try block 
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("File not found.")
    except IOError:
        print("Problem with the file!")
#Step 3: Call the functions
get_stat( get_file() )

This function asks the user to enter the file path until the user enters a file path that could be accessed without any exception. The function returns the file path that could be accessed without any exception.
Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

We need this variable to control when we should stop asking the user to enter the file path. This variable is True when the file path is valid, and False otherwise. We initialize it to False because we have not received the file path yet.

We need to repeat asking the user to enter the file path as long as the user enters a file path that is not valid. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the file path is not valid.

We check whether the file path is not valid by inverting the condition that checks whether the file path is valid. We invert the condition by using the not operator. Note that the following statement is also correct:
while valid == False
Note that the not operator takes a single condition and evaluates to True if that condition is False and to False if the condition is True.

The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters a file path that is not valid. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters a file path that is valid.
The try blocks tries to execute the code within it. The statements in the try block may throw several types of exception.
If an error is encountered, the try block code execution is stopped and transferred down to the except block(s).

The open function opens the file. The variable file_name specifies the path to this file. We want to read the file; therefore, we open it in the read mode "r".
We could also call the open function without specifying the mode, because when only the filename is passed, the open function opens the file in read mode.
We need to close the file after opening it; therefore, we use close() to close it and free up any system resources taken up by the open file.
The statement is executed when none of the previous statements in the try block throw an exception. In this case, the input file path is valid and we set variable valid to True.
We need to handle the FileNotFoundError. This error occurs when the file could not be found.
The body of this except block gets executed only if the file could not be found. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.

We need to handle the IOError. This error occurs when an error occurs when trying to read/close the file.
